newsitem.title: UK: Pearson believes Penguin damage limited.
newsitem.headline: Pearson believes Penguin damage limited.

text.p: Pearson Plc said on Monday that it did not believe the effects of the improper accounting discovered at its Penguin USA subsidiary would spill over into the current year's performance.
"The profits and sales of Penguin going forward should not be affected by this improper accounting," finance director John Makinson told a news conference.

Makinson said that Pearson was confident that the 100 million pounds set aside to cover the costs of the improper accounting, which dates back to 1991, should be enough for "all known and foreseen eventualities".
The problems relate to unauthorised discounts given to customers in return for early payments.

Makinson said that Pearson believed that the problems were the work of "one rogue employee". He said that "there was no firm evidence of collusion" although the employee's superior had been suspended as a precaution.
"We at Pearson are trying to learn the lessons from this," he added, saying that procedures had been tightened in the wake of the problem.
